summary: Validated 3 production features (lot numbering, post-auction down payments, checkout-success seller_contact). 7/9 backend tests pass, 1 minor (Decimal vs float type), and 1 CRITICAL bug uncovered in /api/payments/status/{session_id}: the seller-contact enrichment block references `db.payment_transactions` but never calls `db = get_db()`, so a NameError is silently swallowed by the bare `except Exception: pass`. Net effect: seller_contact will NEVER be returned to the PaymentSuccessPage even when the txn + seller exist. Lot numbering (build_lots_with_end_time) correctly overrides seller-supplied lot_number to 1..N and raises ValueError on >500. Down-payment HTTP layer (GET /me, GET /{auction_id}) returns correct 401/200/404. Down-payment cron (`expire_overdue_down_payments`) is registered in /api/admin/scheduler/status. Down-payment math is correct: storage=$50 flat, vehicle=10% (returns Decimal('1234.57') for 12345.67 — value correct, type is Decimal not float; main agent should confirm intent).

critical.issue: BUG: get_checkout_status() in /app/backend/routes/payments.py (~line 192-233) references `db.payment_transactions.find_one(...)` and `db.users.find_one(...)` but `db` is NEVER assigned inside the function body (other endpoints in the same file all do `db = get_db()` first, e.g., lines 78, 249, 300). The resulting NameError is caught by `except Exception: pass`, so `seller_contact` and `listing_id` are SILENTLY DROPPED from every response. PaymentSuccessPage's [data-testid='checkout-seller-contact'] block will therefore never render in production. FIX: add `db = get_db()` immediately after `import stripe` (or at top of try-block) inside get_checkout_status.

minor.issue: Returns Decimal (e.g., Decimal('1234.57')) for vehicle 10%, while storage returns float 50.0. Inconsistent return type — JSON serialiser handles both via FastAPI but downstream consumers comparing with `==` against a float will fail. Recommend casting to float in the helper for type homogeneity, OR use Decimal everywhere.

No auth guard on this endpoint — any unauthenticated caller who knows/guesses a session_id can read seller email/phone via Stripe + DB lookup. Recommend adding `Depends(security)` and verifying the caller is the buyer on the txn (or admin). Tangential to this sprint but a privacy concern once the `db = get_db()` bug is fixed.

integration_issues.issue: Will never render the [data-testid='checkout-seller-contact'] card until the backend `db = get_db()` bug above is fixed. The frontend defensive `paymentInfo?.seller_contact &&` chaining is correct — page renders cleanly when null.

/app/backend/services/listings_service.py build_lots_with_end_time: hard-codes `timedelta(minutes=idx)` for stagger. Future-proof: read stagger interval from marketplace_settings (some auction houses use 30-second stagger for fast-paced sales).

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: Refactor introduced post-sale seller-contact enrichment in get_checkout_status without the standard `db = get_db()` initialisation that every other endpoint in payments.py uses. The enrichment was wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass` to make it 'best-effort' (per main-agent UX requirement that the success page must never break). However, the very first reference inside the try-block — `db.payment_transactions.find_one(...)` — raises NameError because `db` is undefined. The bare except swallows it, the success page renders without seller_contact, and there are no logs to indicate anything went wrong. REPRODUCTION: 1) Pay any listing via Stripe Checkout. 2) Land on /payment/success?session_id=cs_xxx. 3) Inspect the response from /api/payments/status/{session_id}: it returns {status, payment_status:'paid', amount_total, ...} with NO seller_contact key, even when the matching payment_transactions row + seller user both exist. MITIGATION: One-line fix — insert `db = get_db()` after the `import stripe` line (or as the first statement of the try-block). Additionally: replace `except Exception: pass` with `except Exception as e: logger.warning('seller_contact enrichment failed: %s', e)` so the next regression of this kind is observable.
